records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֣א בְאָזְנַ֗י ק֤וֹל גָּדוֹל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר קָרְב֖וּ פְּקֻדּ֣וֹת הָעִ֑יר וְאִ֛ישׁ כְּלִ֥י מַשְׁחֵת֖וֹ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he called in my ears [with] a loud voice, saying, Draw near, executioners of the city, and each his weapon of destruction in his hand.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cried out in my hearing with a loud voice, "Come near, you who are appointed to punish the city, each with his weapon of destruction in his hand!"

L.1: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called in my ears with a loud voice, saying, "Draw near, you who are to punish the city, each [with] his weapon of destruction in his hand!"

R.1: Then I heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} shout in a loud voice, "Come here, you who will punish the city! Each of you, bring a weapon to destroy it!"

decisions.choice: draw near, you who are to punish the city: a summons to those appointed for judgment
alternatives: the punishments of the city have drawn near: a statement, not a command
decisions.reason: The verb can be a command ("draw near") or a statement ("they have drawn near"), and the noun can mean "those in charge of" or "the punishments of" the city. Since six armed men appear at once (9:2), the cry is read as a summons to them. The other reading also fits: the day of reckoning for the city has come (7:7, 12).

decisions.choice: he called in my ears with a loud voice: an answer to 8:18
decisions.reason: In 8:18 the LORD said that the people would cry "in my ears with a loud voice" and he would not listen. Now it is the LORD who cries out with a loud voice, calling the judgment.

decisions.choice: you who are appointed to punish the city (B); you who will punish the city (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the sense of people put in charge of the city's punishment (m1). Readable keeps it short.

records.heading: Six men with weapons

records.source: וְהִנֵּ֣ה שִׁשָּׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֡ים בָּאִ֣ים׀מִדֶּרֶךְ־שַׁ֨עַר הָעֶלְי֜וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀מָפְנֶ֣ה צָפ֗וֹנָה וְאִ֨ישׁ כְּלִ֤י מַפָּצוֹ֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ וְאִישׁ־אֶחָ֤ד בְּתוֹכָם֙ לָבֻ֣שׁ בַּדִּ֔ים וְקֶ֥סֶת הַסֹּפֵ֖ר בְּמָתְנָ֑יו וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ וַיַּ֣עַמְד֔וּ אֵ֖צֶל מִזְבַּ֥ח הַנְּחֹֽשֶׁת׃
records.gloss: And behold, six men coming from [the] direction of [the] gate the upper which faces north, and each his weapon of smashing in his hand, and one man in their midst clothed [in] linen, and [the] writing case of the scribe at his waist; and they went in and stood beside [the] altar of the bronze.
pieces: Then six men came from the direction of the upper gate that faces north, each with a weapon for smashing in his hand. Among them was a man dressed in linen, with a scribe's writing case at his side. They came in and took their places beside the bronze altar.

L.2: And look, six men were coming by way of the upper gate that faces north, each with his weapon for smashing in his hand; and among them [was] one man clothed in linen, with a scribe's writing case at his waist. And they went in and stood beside the bronze altar.

R.2: Then I saw six men coming from the upper gate, the one that faces north. Each of them held a weapon for smashing. With them was a man dressed in linen clothes. He carried a scribe's writing kit at his side. They came in and stood beside the bronze altar.

decisions.choice: six men and one man in linen: heavenly agents sent to carry out the judgment
decisions.reason: Like the destroyer of Exodus 12:23 and the angel of 2 Samuel 24:16, these are messengers of God's judgment, though the text calls them "men". The one dressed in linen is set apart from the six. Linen was the dress of priests (Leviticus 16:4) and of the heavenly messenger in Daniel 10:5 and 12:6-7.

decisions.choice: a scribe's writing case: the scribe's kit, worn at the belt
decisions.reason: A scribe carried a case or palette holding ink and reed pens, tucked into his belt at his side. The man in linen needs it to mark the faithful (9:4).

decisions.choice: the upper gate and the bronze altar of the temple
decisions.reason: King Jotham built "the upper gate of the house of the LORD" (2 Kings 15:35), probably this north gate. The bronze altar was Solomon's altar, which King Ahaz had moved to the north side to make room for an altar of his own (2 Kings 16:14). The men stand where the scenes of chapter 8 took place.

decisions.choice: a scribe's writing kit
alternatives: the writing case of the scribe
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer word for the case of pens and ink (m2).

records.source: וּכְב֣וֹד׀אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל נַעֲלָה֙ מֵעַ֤ל הַכְּרוּב֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה עָלָ֔יו אֶ֖ל מִפְתַּ֣ן הַבָּ֑יִת וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֶל־הָאִישׁ֙ הַלָּבֻ֣שׁ הַבַּדִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֛ר קֶ֥סֶת הַסֹּפֵ֖ר בְּמָתְנָֽיו׃ס
records.gloss: And [the] glory of [the] God of Israel went up from upon the cherub which it had been upon it, to [the] threshold of the house; and he called to the man the clothed [in] the linen who [had] the writing case of the scribe at his waist.
pieces: Now the glory of the God of Israel had risen from above the cherub where it had rested, and had moved to the threshold of the temple. He called to the man dressed in linen who had the writing case at his side.

L.3: Now the glory of the God of Israel had gone up from the cherub on which it had been, to the threshold of the house. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called to the man clothed in linen, at whose waist [was] the scribe's writing case.

R.3: The glory of the God of Israel rose up from above the cherub where it had been. It moved to the doorway of the temple. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} called to the man dressed in linen who had the writing kit at his side.

decisions.choice: the cherub: the winged figures over the ark, above which the LORD was enthroned
decisions.reason: In the most holy place of Solomon's temple two great cherubim stood with outspread wings over the ark (1 Kings 6:23-28; 8:6-7), and the LORD was called the one "enthroned on the cherubim" (1 Samuel 4:4; Psalm 80:2). The singular here may mean the pair, or the cherubim of the glory itself; chapter 10 describes them (see 10:1).

decisions.choice: the glory moves to the threshold: the first step of its departure from the temple
decisions.reason: The glory leaves its place in stages: to the threshold (here and 10:4), to the east gate (10:18-19), and out of the city to the mountain on the east (11:22-23). In 43:1-5 it returns by the same east gate.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} called
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker, as the next verse does, so that "he" is not taken as the glory or the cherub.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלָ֔יו עֲבֹר֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעִ֔יר בְּת֖וֹךְ יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְהִתְוִ֨יתָ תָּ֜ו עַל־מִצְח֣וֹת הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הַנֶּֽאֱנָחִים֙ וְהַנֶּ֣אֱנָקִ֔ים עַ֚ל כָּל־הַתּ֣וֹעֵב֔וֹת הַֽנַּעֲשׂ֖וֹת בְּתוֹכָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to him, Go through [the] midst of the city, through [the] midst of Jerusalem, and mark a mark on [the] foreheads of the men who sigh and groan over all the abominations that are done in its midst.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "Go all through the city, all through Jerusalem, and put a mark on the foreheads of the {{gender:people|men}} who sigh and groan over all the detestable practices committed in it."

L.4: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "Pass into the midst of the city, into the midst of Jerusalem, and put a mark on the foreheads of the {{gender:people|men}} who sigh and groan over all the abominations that are done in its midst."

R.4: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "Go through the whole city of Jerusalem. Put a mark on the forehead of everyone who is sad and groaning over all the disgusting things being done there."

decisions.choice: a mark: the Hebrew is the name of the letter taw, which was written as a simple cross
decisions.reason: The word is the name of the last letter of the Hebrew alphabet. In the old Hebrew script it had the shape of an X or a cross, so the mark was a simple sign, like a signature (Job 31:35 uses the word for a signature). Later readers, Jewish and Christian, drew meanings from its shape, but the text says only that it marks those to be spared.

decisions.choice: the mark on the foreheads: those who belong to God are spared, as in Exodus 12:13 and Revelation 7:3; 9:4
decisions.reason: As the blood on the doorposts spared Israel's houses in Egypt (Exodus 12:13), the mark spares these people. Revelation 7:3 and 9:4 take up the picture: the servants of God are sealed on their foreheads before the judgment falls.

decisions.choice: those who sigh and groan: the people who grieve over the city's sins, not only those who avoid them
decisions.reason: Judgment does not fall on everyone alike. The LORD distinguishes those who mourn over what is done in Jerusalem from those who do it, as Abraham asked that the righteous not be swept away with the wicked (Genesis 18:23-25). Chapter 18 makes the same point in teaching.

decisions.choice: the {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for "men" here means people: the sparing is not limited to men, as the list of those to be struck in 9:6 shows. Readable says "everyone", which needs no setting.

records.heading: A mark on the foreheads

records.source: וּלְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ אָמַ֣ר בְּאָזְנַ֔י עִבְר֥וּ בָעִ֛יר אַחֲרָ֖יו וְהַכּ֑וּ אַל־תָּחֹ֥ס עֵינְכֶ֖ם וְאַל־תַּחְמֹֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: And to these he said in my ears, Pass through the city after him and strike; [let] not spare your eye, and do not have pity.
pieces: To the others {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said in my hearing, "Follow him through the city and strike. Do not look on them with pity or spare them.

L.5: And to the others {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said in my hearing, "Pass through the city after him and strike! Let your eye not pity, and do not spare.

R.5: Then I heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} say to the others, "Follow him through the city and kill. Do not feel sorry for them or show them mercy.

decisions.choice: let your eye not pity, and do not spare: the words of 8:18 and 5:11, now given to the executioners
decisions.reason: The LORD said in 8:18 that his eye would not spare. The same words are now his command to the six men.

decisions.choice: kill
decisions.reason: "Strike" here means strike dead, as 9:6-7 make plain; Readable says "kill".

records.source: זָקֵ֡ן בָּח֣וּר וּבְתוּלָה֩ וְטַ֨ף וְנָשִׁ֜ים תַּהַרְג֣וּ לְמַשְׁחִ֗ית וְעַל־כָּל־אִ֨ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־עָלָ֤יו הַתָּו֙ אַל־תִּגַּ֔שׁוּ וּמִמִּקְדָּשִׁ֖י תָּחֵ֑לּוּ וַיָּחֵ֨לּוּ֙ בָּאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הַזְּקֵנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֥י הַבָּֽיִת׃
records.gloss: Old man, young man and young woman, and little children and women, kill to destruction; but upon any man who [has] upon him the mark, do not come near; and from my sanctuary begin. And they began with the men, the elders, who [were] before the house.
pieces: Kill old men, young men and young women, little children and women, until none are left; but do not go near anyone who has the mark. Start at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary." So they began with the elders standing in front of the temple.

L.6: Old man, young man and young woman, little children and women, kill to destruction; but do not come near anyone on whom [is] the mark. And begin from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary." So they began with the men, the elders, who [were] in front of the house.

R.6: Kill them all: old men, young men and young women, women and little children. But do not touch anyone who has the mark. Start at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} temple." So they started with the elders who were in front of the temple.

decisions.choice: begin from my sanctuary: judgment starts where the sin was worst, in God's own house
decisions.reason: The abominations of chapter 8 were done in the temple, so the judgment starts there. 1 Peter 4:17 says, in another setting, that judgment begins with the household of God.

decisions.choice: the elders in front of the house: the leaders seen in chapter 8
decisions.reason: The text does not say which group is meant. The twenty-five men of 8:16 stood in front of the temple, and the seventy elders of 8:11 were the city's leaders; either way, the judgment starts with those who led the worship of other gods.

decisions.choice: kill to destruction: kill completely
decisions.reason: The phrase means killing that leaves no one, except those who bear the mark.

decisions.choice: until none are left (B); Kill them all (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "to destruction" means (m3). Readable puts the command first and lists those it includes after it.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם טַמְּא֣וּ אֶת־הַבַּ֗יִת וּמַלְא֧וּ אֶת־הַחֲצֵר֛וֹת חֲלָלִ֖ים צֵ֑אוּ וְיָצְא֖וּ וְהִכּ֥וּ בָעִֽיר׃
records.gloss: And he said to them, Defile the house, and fill the courts [with the] slain. Go out! And they went out and struck in the city.
pieces: He said to them, "Defile the temple and fill its courts with the dead. Go!" So they went out and struck people down throughout the city.

L.7: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Defile the house! Fill the courts [with] slain! Go out!" So they went out and struck [them] down in the city.

R.7: He told them, "Make the temple unclean by filling its courtyards with dead bodies. Now go!" So they went out and killed people all through the city.

decisions.choice: defile the house: a dead body made a place unclean for worship
decisions.reason: Under the law, contact with a corpse made a person or place unclean (Numbers 19:11-16). The people had already defiled the sanctuary with their idols (5:11); now the LORD himself orders it filled with the dead, a sign that he is abandoning it.

decisions.choice: Make the temple unclean by filling its courtyards with dead bodies
alternatives: Defile the house, and fill the courts with the slain
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two commands to show how the temple is defiled (m1).

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ כְּהַכּוֹתָ֔ם וְנֵֽאשֲׁאַ֖ר אָ֑נִי וָאֶפְּלָ֨ה עַל־פָּנַ֜י וָאֶזְעַ֗ק וָֽאֹמַר֙ אֲהָהּ֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הֲמַשְׁחִ֣ית אַתָּ֗ה אֵ֚ת כָּל־שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּשָׁפְכְּךָ֥ אֶת־חֲמָתְךָ֖ עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: And it was, while they were striking and I was left, and I fell on my face and cried out and said, Ah, Lord Yahweh! [Are] destroying you all [the] remnant of Israel in your pouring out your wrath on Jerusalem?
pieces: While they were striking them down and I was left alone, I fell on my face and cried out, "Oh, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} destroy all who remain of Israel as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} pour out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wrath on Jerusalem?"

L.8: And it came about, while they were striking and I was left [alone], that I fell on my face and cried out and said, "Ah, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} destroying all the remnant of Israel, as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} pour out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wrath on Jerusalem?"

R.8: While they were killing people, I was left there alone. I threw myself face down on the ground and cried out, "Oh no, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} going to destroy everyone left in Israel as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} pour out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger on Jerusalem?"

decisions.choice: Ah: a cry of grief and alarm before God
decisions.reason: The same cry opens Jeremiah's protest in Jeremiah 1:6 and 4:10, and Ezekiel's in 4:14 and 11:13. It is a plea, not a complaint against God.

decisions.choice: I was left: Ezekiel alone among the dead in the temple
decisions.reason: The verb form is unusual, but the sense is that Ezekiel was left standing alone while the killing went on around him.

decisions.choice: the remnant of Israel: those still left in the land after the exile of 597 BC
decisions.reason: After King Jehoiachin and the leading citizens were taken to Babylon, Jerusalem and Judah were all that remained of the people in the land. Ezekiel fears that this judgment will leave no one. He asks the same question again in 11:13.

decisions.choice: Oh (B); Oh no (R)
decisions.reason: The cry follows Jeremiah 1:6: "Ah" at Literal, "Oh" at Balanced, "Oh no" at Readable.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י עֲוֺ֨ן בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל וִֽיהוּדָה֙ גָּדוֹל֙ בִּמְאֹ֣ד מְאֹ֔ד וַתִּמָּלֵ֤א הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ דָּמִ֔ים וְהָעִ֖יר מָלְאָ֣ה מֻטֶּ֑ה כִּ֣י אָמְר֗וּ עָזַ֤ב יְהוָה֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאֵ֥ין יְהוָ֖ה רֹאֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, [The] guilt of [the] house of Israel and Judah [is] great, very, very; and the land is filled [with] blood, and the city is full of perversion; for they say, Has forsaken Yahweh the land, and Yahweh [is] not seeing.
pieces: He said to me, "The guilt of the house of Israel and Judah is immense. The land is full of bloodshed and the city full of injustice. For they say, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has abandoned the land; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does not see.'"

L.9: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Great, very, very [great is] the iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah; and the land is filled [with] blood, and the city is full of perversion. For they say, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has forsaken the land, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is not seeing.'"

R.9: He answered me, "The people of Israel and Judah have sinned terribly. The land is full of murder, and the city is full of injustice. They say, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has left the land. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} does not see.'"

decisions.choice: "The LORD has forsaken the land; the LORD does not see": the elders' words of 8:12, given back as the charge
decisions.reason: The LORD repeats the saying of 8:12, with its two halves turned around. What the leaders said to excuse their idols becomes the reason for the judgment: they thought the LORD did not see, but he has seen everything.

decisions.choice: perversion: twisting of justice
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It comes from a verb meaning "to bend" or "to turn aside", used of turning justice aside (Exodus 23:6; Deuteronomy 16:19). Together with the bloodshed it describes a city where the courts protect the guilty.

decisions.choice: iniquity (L); guilt (B); sinned (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this word in the prophets: "iniquity" at Literal, "guilt" at Balanced, "sin" at Readable. The saying keeps the wording of 8:12 at each level.

decisions.choice: Great, very, very [great is] the iniquity
decisions.reason: Literal puts "great" first to keep the doubled "very" together with it and to read as an exclamation; the Hebrew puts it after the subject.

records.source: וְגַ֨ם־אֲנִ֔י לֹא־תָח֥וֹס עֵינִ֖י וְלֹ֣א אֶחְמֹ֑ל דַּרְכָּ֖ם בְּרֹאשָׁ֥ם נָתָֽתִּי׃
records.gloss: And as for me also, will not spare my eye, and not I will have pity; their way on their head I will put.
pieces: As for me, I will not look on them with pity or spare them; I will bring their conduct down on their own heads."

L.10: And as for me too, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eye will not pity, and I will not spare; I will bring their way down on their heads."

R.10: So I will not feel sorry for them or show them mercy. I will pay them back for what they have done."

decisions.choice: I will bring their way on their heads: I will make their own conduct fall back on them
decisions.reason: Their "way" is how they have lived. The punishment is the result of what they have done, coming back on them; the expression returns in 11:21; 16:43 and 22:31.

decisions.choice: I will pay them back for what they have done
alternatives: I will bring their way down on their heads
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means (m1), and keeps the wording of 8:18 for the first half.

records.source: וְהִנֵּ֞ה הָאִ֣ישׁ׀לְבֻ֣שׁ הַבַּדִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר הַקֶּ֨סֶת֙ בְּמָתְנָ֔יו מֵשִׁ֥יב דָּבָ֖ר לֵאמֹ֑ר עָשִׂ֕יתִי כְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥רצִוִּיתָֽנִי׃ס
records.gloss: And behold, the man clothed [in] the linen, who [had] the writing case at his waist, brought back word, saying, I have done according to all that you commanded me.
pieces: Then the man dressed in linen, with the writing case at his side, came back with a report: "I have done as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} commanded me."

L.11: And look, the man clothed in linen, with the writing case at his waist, brought back word, saying, "I have done as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} commanded me."

R.11: Then the man dressed in linen, who had the writing kit at his side, came back and reported, "I have done what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} commanded me."

decisions.choice: as you commanded me: the written text and the text as read differ slightly
alternatives: according to all that you commanded me
decisions.reason: The consonants of the Hebrew text read "as you commanded me"; the scribes' marginal reading has "according to all that you commanded me". The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: "I have done as you commanded": the marking of the faithful is finished
decisions.reason: The report shows that the command of 9:4 has been carried out: those who grieved over the city have been marked and spared. The same man is sent next to scatter fire over the city (10:2).
